A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Multilevel Control Functional, with matching methods, experiments, and Appendices A–D. The text, equations, figures, tables, and proofs are available and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original integration-error experiments, Lotka–Volterra Bayesian inference results, and Bayesian neural-network ELBO and test log-likelihood results in Section 4 and Appendix D.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results and adds an MLBQ comparison, an ODE kernel sensitivity experiment, and numerical summaries of the neural-network results.

M1.justification: The MLCF estimator, sample-allocation procedure, simplified estimator, and MLCFRG extension remain unchanged in Section 3 and Appendix B. The added kernel experiment evaluates options already described in Appendix C.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the illustrative ODE, synthetic RKHS example, boundary-value ODE, hare–lynx Lotka–Volterra inference, and wine-quality-red neural-network regression. The added comparisons retain these datasets and task requirements.

E2.justification: v4 adds multilevel Bayesian quadrature (MLBQ, Li et al., 2023) to the boundary-value ODE comparison in Section 4, Figure 3, and Appendix D.3. v3 compares against MLMC and CF there; the earlier comparators remain.

E3.justification: Appendix D.3 adds a controlled kernel and length-scale selection experiment using i.i.d. samples and the existing Table 3 allocations and budgets of 0.30, 0.91, and 1.52 seconds. Settings for the retained experiments are unchanged.

E4.justification: New Figure 8 tests ODE sensitivity to squared-exponential versus preconditioned kernels and marginal-likelihood versus median-heuristic length-scale selection. The existing neural-network kernel and sample-size analyses remain, with v3 Figures 8–11 becoming v4 Figures 9–12.

E5.justification: Both retain the stated 50-replication experiments, 100 ODE repetitions, and ten neural-network runs with standard deviations. Tables 5–6 provide numerical summaries using the existing reporting practice; no increased run counts or new uncertainty procedure are stated.

E6.justification: v4 adds MLBQ error distributions in Figure 3 and kernel sensitivity results in Figure 8. Tables 5–6 newly tabulate neural-network scores; for 20 hidden units, test log-likelihood is -386.57 ± 0.3 for MLCFRG and -386.27 ± 0.1 for MLMCRG. These summarize existing settings, without establishing a performance change from v3.

T1.justification: Assumptions A1–A8, the theoretical statements in Section 3, and Appendix B proofs are retained. Equation 10 replaces a stray y with x' in a kernel argument, a notation correction without revised mathematical reasoning or theoretical results.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about combining control functionals with multilevel structure, variance bounds, optimal allocation, broad applicability, and variational inference. The additional experiments support these existing claims.

C2.justification: The convergence and allocation interpretations, cubic-cost limitation, smoothness dependence, and reliance on fidelity hierarchies remain unchanged. Appendix D retains its caveat about unmet assumptions. The new kernel findings support the already-described median heuristic without introducing a new mechanism or applicability boundary.

D1.justification: v4 adds a reproducibility statement saying core code is released in supplementary materials; v3 has no corresponding statement. Appendix D.3 also specifies the added sensitivity experiment's kernel choices, tuning rules, and reuse of Table 3 sample allocations.

R1.justification: v4 adds citations and references to Sun's 2023 thesis on transfer learning in Monte Carlo and Li's 2024 thesis on multilevel integration and tsunami modelling. The main research positioning is retained; the swapped Sun et al. 2023a/b labels identify existing works.

P1.justification: v4 updates affiliations and publication headers, adds acknowledgments, ethics/reproducibility and LLM-use statements, and makes limited explanatory and notation edits. The main narrative and section ordering remain substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: The ICLR template changes the title, headers, spacing, and figure sizing. Figure 3 gains an MLBQ series, Figure 8 and Tables 5–6 are added, and retained appendix displays are relocated or renumbered. New Figure 8 incorrectly describes its linear vertical axis as logarithmic.

improvement.justification: v4 supplies a relevant MLBQ comparison missing from v3, adds an ODE kernel sensitivity check, and makes existing neural-network outcomes easier to assess through Tables 5–6. These modestly improve empirical support and transparency, outweighing Figure 8's minor caption error. The core method and theory remain unchanged.
